sources.title: Transitional rules for the 2024 GST rate change
Do I need to register for GST?
Basic guide to corporate income tax for companies

regimes.name: Standard GST candidate
regimes.applicability: Ordinary taxable local supplies by a GST-registered business.
conditions: Apply current time-of-supply and rate-transition rules.
Compulsory registration considers calendar-year turnover or expected next-12-month taxable turnover above SGD 1 million.
Verify the effective registration date; prospective-registration timing changed for liabilities arising from 1 July 2025.
Input tax requires eligible business purpose, invoices/import evidence and no blocked category.

regimes.name: Zero-rated exports/international services candidate
regimes.applicability: Qualifying goods exports or prescribed international services.
conditions: Zero-rated supplies remain taxable; input recovery remains conditional.
Retain required export evidence; foreign payment or customer address alone is not proof.

regimes.name: GST exemption classification
regimes.applicability: Specified exempt supplies, including defined financial/residential-property/IPM/digital-token categories.
conditions: An industry label does not establish exemption.
Related input tax is generally not claimable; partial-exemption and de minimis rules need review.

regimes.name: Company/business income-tax review
regimes.applicability: Income-tax computation by entity and year of assessment; never a checkout tax.
conditions: IRAS states a 17% company headline rate; deductions, exemptions and rebates need entity/year review.
Sole proprietorships and partnerships are not companies for this purpose.

classification_questions: Which charges are meals, takeaway goods, catering, delivery, alcohol, tips or service charges?
How are discounts, deposits, vouchers and refunds treated at the relevant tax point?
How do service charges, tips, delivery fees, vouchers and GST-inclusive price displays affect the tax base?
Which receipts are subscriptions, joining fees, donations, facility hire, food or admissions?
What is the club's legal form and which activities are commercial supplies?
Does a customer's blocked input claim on sports/recreation subscriptions differ from the club's output-tax liability?
Which individual products are medicines, medical devices, supplements or cosmetics?
Does the business also provide clinical services, manufacture goods or import them?
Is there an evidenced statutory exception, rather than an assumed general medicine exemption?
Does the business act as principal, agent, importer, exporter or manufacturer?
Which tariff/product codes and documentary evidence support each treatment?
Do customer-accounting, gross-margin or import schemes apply to the actual goods?
Are sales on own account, consignment or commission, and is there a manufacturer appointment?
How are rebates, returns, free stock and cross-border transactions documented?
Are export records sufficient and who is the importer of record?
Which SKU classifications apply to the actual product mix?
Are there bundled goods/services, gift vouchers, used goods or imports?
Are prices GST-inclusive and is any used-goods/customer-accounting scheme applicable?
Are parts, labor, consumables, subcontract work and warranties separately supplied or bundled?
Does the workshop repair, manufacture, import or export goods?
Are parts/labor local supplies, and is any international-service claim legally supported?

open_questions: Confirm GST registration dates, voluntary-registration conditions, invoice/price-display rules and current InvoiceNow requirements for the business.
Review club output supplies separately from the customer's input restriction; sports/recreation subscription input claims are specifically blocked under IRAS guidance.
Assess mixed exempt/taxable input allocation, imported-service reverse charge and any product-specific or margin/customer-accounting scheme.
Do not infer GST exemption for pharmacy/health products from another country's law; confirm each exception.
Confirm the applicable accounting framework, entity income-tax basis and current rebates independently.
